`deadlineMs` is set from the scenario options' wall-clock time limit — `options.timeLimitMs` — at the point where `armArgs` is assembled in `runScenario` (eval/src/loop.ts), as `deadlineMs: Date.now() + options.timeLimitMs`.

That construction is what feeds the per-turn guard you can see in both arm loops (native and context-tree):

```ts
for (let turnIndex = 0; turnIndex < args.options.maxTurns; turnIndex += 1) {
  if (Date.now() >= args.deadlineMs) return { status: 'time_cap', finalText };
```

So the two caps in `armArgs` are distinct: `options.maxTurns` bounds iterations (and produces the `turn_cap` status you saw on the 40-turn native failures), while `deadlineMs` derives from `options.timeLimitMs` and produces the `time_cap` status — the wall-clock backstop that fires independently of turn count. In all 56 recorded runs neither arm ever hit `time_cap`; every cap-out in the dataset was `turn_cap`.
